findings.title: The NCAA Rule 7 scoring engine is fully built, sourced, tested - and wired to nothing
evidence: packages/core/src/lib/ncaaScoringRules.ts is 1401 lines: 14 meet formats, exhibition isolation (7-10-1), DQ place advancement (7-7), tie division (7-8), lost-place accounting, per-format maxScorersPerTeam.
grep across the monorepo for every export returns exactly two consumers: its own test file and a re-export in packages/core/src/index.ts. Zero product code calls it.

The product scores via calculatePoints in packages/core/src/lib/utils.ts against the legacy ScoringSettings shape (consumers: scoringEngine, rosterOptimizer, arbitrage/*, scenarioDiff, matrix swimCloudMeetImportBridge).

Provenance verified this session: data/scoring_rules/sources/ncaascoring.pdf sha256 5b98f8f69470606ea179b053b86d7fb4451f61a874c0fff5d8d18b369d6bb92e is byte-identical to a fresh fetch of https://meets.swimdna.org/media/ncaascoring.pdf and matches the manifest.
findings.consequence: ScoringSettings models relay points as a scalar relayMultiplier. That is exactly correct for all six championship field sizes (relay table is 2x individual at 6/8/12/16/18/24 - all verified against the rulebook). It is structurally WRONG for every non-championship format: dual 6+ lanes is individual 9-4-3-2-1 with relays 11-4-2 (11 is not 2x9); dual <=5 lanes is 5-3-1 with relays 7 (7 is not 2x5). The three dual diving tables (7-1-4) are also inexpressible - diving is modelled only as diverScorerWeight, not as its own place-value table. A dual meet is the most common format in college swimming and the app cannot represent one today.

findings.title: Every captured page is cacheStatus 'provisional'; a re-crawl re-fetches all of it
evidence: data/swimcloud-captures/captures/meet-356467.json: 234/234 pages cacheStatus='provisional'. No page is ever promoted to durable.

Measured wall time from retrievedAt timestamps: meetTeamSwims 42 pages/122s (2981ms observed gap), teamRoster 8 pages/21s (3002ms gap), swimmerTimes 184 pages/75s (409ms gap, pooled 3 lanes). Total ~218s for 4 teams.
findings.consequence: 50 sequential pages cost more wall-clock than 184 pooled ones, so the 3000ms floor dominates - and the user has ruled out relaxing it (d3). Durable caching is therefore the main available speedup, and it strictly REDUCES traffic rather than adding detection surface.

findings.title: SwimCloud import silently drops the best swimmers (prelims/finals ambiguity)
evidence: SwimCloud team-swims pages carry no round column; a finalist appears as 2+ near-identical rows whose Place is a per-round placement (proven: a 1:47.40 marked 2nd vs a 1:47.77 marked 1st).

The landed fix excludes the entire ambiguous group from the import rather than guessing a winner - correct per the provenance rules, but 13 of 30 rows (43%) on the one measured page were in such a group.
findings.consequence: The better a swimmer is, the more likely they vanish from an opponent-scouting import. Directly undermines user decision d1's scouting/projection requirement. Candidate fix: use meetEvent pages, which do carry round context, as a disambiguation SOURCE (not a guess).

openDecisions.question: How should the Rule 7 engine (ncaaScoringRules.ts) and the legacy ScoringSettings converge?
openDecisions.optionA: Replace: make calculatePoints delegate to computeNcaaEventScoring. One engine, no duplication, every format correct by construction. But it rewrites the scoring data path that NSISC totals are byte-exact verified against, and that optimizer/arbitrage/scenario-diff all depend on. Highest risk before a deadline.
openDecisions.optionB: Extend: add optional relayPoints[] / divingPoints[] / per-team per-event place caps to ScoringSettings, and GENERATE the built-in presets from NCAA_FORMAT_RULESETS so the tables still live in exactly one place. calculatePoints keeps its structure and learns to prefer relayPoints over relayMultiplier when present. Additive, every existing verified behaviour preserved, every format expressible. Recommended.
openDecisions.recommendation: B, with A recorded as the longer-term convergence once the deadline passes.
